# Implement version read + dimmed right-aligned header display

## Summary
Read the plugin version at runtime from `packages/herdr/package.json` and render it as a dimmed, right-aligned `v<version>` suffix in the work item selection list header, without disturbing the left-aligned title.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A runtime helper reads the plugin version from `packages/herdr/package.json` (JSON parse via `readFileSync`, following the `shortcut-config.ts` pattern); when the file is missing or unparseable it falls back gracefully (e.g. `'?'` or omit) without throwing.
- The list-mode header renders `v<version>` right-aligned to `cols` (visible-width padding computed with ANSI codes stripped before padding), dimmed via `ANSI.dim`, matching the `[auto-refresh on]` treatment; the left-aligned `Work Items — N item(s)` title is unchanged.
- The version is read at runtime from the manifest, not hardcoded in the renderer (stays in sync with the manifest version).
- On narrow panes where the suffix would overlap the title, the suffix is dropped or truncated (guard on `cols`) — no layout breakage, no overflow beyond the pane width.
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes, including the header version tests (F1).

## Minimal Implementation
- Add a small version-read helper in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (or a sibling module) using the `readFileSync`/`dirname` pattern from `shortcut-config.ts`, with a safe fallback.
- In the list-mode header renderer (near line ~1585): compute the header's visible width, pad to `cols`, and append the dimmed `v<version>` suffix right-aligned; reuse `truncateLine`/visible-length logic; guard on `cols` for narrow panes.
- Keep the renderer testable via the existing `readFile`-style injection seam where practical.

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: header version rendering tests (F1) — test-first ordering.

## Deliverables
- Updated `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`; version helper; no change to `packages/herdr/package.json` (version source only).

# Differentiate the background of the In Review header

## Problem statement

In the Herdr work-item selection list, all group section headers (e.g. `── Group 1 (4) ▼ ──`, `── Idea (2) ──`, `── In Review (5) ──`) are rendered identically — bold, with a foreground stage colour and no background fill. The producer cannot distinguish the In Review section from other sections at a glance, which matters because In Review items are the only ones with an active producer-review obligation. Give the In Review header a grey background so the section stands out visually.

## Users

- **Herdr users (primarily the producer / session operator)** who scan the selection list for the In Review queue and need to locate that section quickly.
  - User story: "As a Herdr user reviewing the selection list, I want the In Review header to have a distinctive grey background so I can spot the review queue section immediately, even when the list is long."

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The group heading row whose label is `In Review` renders with a grey background fill (ANSI 256-colour, e.g. `ANSI.bg(238)` or a nearby grey value) in addition to its current bold/foreground styling.
- AC2: All other group heading rows (e.g. `Group N`, `Idea`, `Completed`, etc.) are unchanged — no background fill added.
- AC3: The selected-heading highlight still works: when the In Review heading is the current selection, the existing reverse-video selection bar (`reverseWrap`) remains visible on top of the grey background.
- AC4: Heading text, count, collapse arrow, and width-truncation behaviour are unaffected by the background change (single-row heading invariant preserved).
- AC5: Unit tests cover the new rendering: a heading with label `In Review` contains the background escape sequence, and other headings do not; existing heading-render tests still pass.
- AC6: Full project test suite passes with the change.
- AC7: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- Use existing ANSI helpers in `worklist.ts` (`ANSI.bg(code)` with a 256-colour code) — no new dependencies.
- Must not change the display-rows model, navigation, collapse logic, or line-count invariants (WL-0MSL5MPSZ003TG94).
- Implementation must be keyed off the heading's `groupLabel === 'In Review'` (the label originates in `grouping.ts`); keep the label source as the single source of truth.

## Existing state

- Group heading rows are first-class rows in the display-rows model (`DisplayHeadingRow`), interleaved by `WorkItemListState.getDisplayRows()` (WL-0MSL5MPSZ003TG94).
- The heading row is rendered in `createListRenderer` at `worklist.ts:~4482`:
  `const line = `${indent} ${ANSI.fg(stageColor(undefined))}${ANSI.bold}── ${row.groupLabel} (${row.count}) ${arrow} ──${ANSI.reset}``
- `ANSI.bg(code)` exists at `worklist.ts:~345` (`\x1b[48;5;${code}m`) and is already used for banner fills (e.g. `ANSI.bg(196)`, `ANSI.bg(220)`, `ANSI.bg(40)`).
- The `In Review` group label is assigned in `grouping.ts:~309` (`groupLabel: 'In Review'` for `stage === 'in_review'`).
- Selected rows are wrapped with `reverseWrap` (re-asserts `\x1b[0m` resets to keep the whole selected row highlighted); heading rows have no interior resets so they are handled fine.

## Desired change

- In the heading-row render branch of `createListRenderer`, when `row.groupLabel === 'In Review'`, wrap the line's base style with a grey background (`${ANSI.bg(238)}` or similar), keeping the existing foreground/bold styling and the existing `reverseWrap` interaction on selection. Other headings render as today.

## Key Files:

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — heading-row render branch (`createListRenderer`, ~line 4482); add conditional grey background for `groupLabel === 'In Review'`; `ANSI.bg` helper at ~line 345.
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` — source of the `In Review` group label (~line 309); reference/consistency only.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-renderer-headings.test.ts` — extend with tests asserting the background escape sequence on `In Review` headings and its absence on others.
- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` — `stageColor`/ANSI conventions (context only).

## Risks & assumptions

- Grey background may reduce contrast against the 220 (yellow-ish) foreground `stageColor` for in-review headings; mitigate by choosing a dark grey (238) and verifying readability. If contrast is insufficient, the foreground can be switched to white (231) for this heading only — record the choice in the implementation.
- Selection visibility: reverse-wrap must stay visible over the background — covered by AC3; verify selection rendering in a terminal, not just by string matching.
- Scope creep: do NOT extend the background to other headings unless separately requested — that is a separate work item (recorded here to avoid accidental bundling).
- Test brittleness: assert on the presence of the `\x1b[48;5;...m` background sequence for the In Review heading rather than on exact full-row strings, to avoid coupling to foreground/bold detail changes.

## Related work

- **Duplicate check performed** — no overlapping completed item found. Related completed items (none duplicates): WL-0MS4FIEN40037GB9 (total actionable count in Herdr header), WL-0MV6JGVPH009YDXB (in_progress/in_review in mandatory In Review set), WL-0MSBVS4AS006ZQEZ (selection-list refresh on tab focus), WL-0MSL5MPSZ003TG94 (heading rows as first-class display rows — this feature builds on that model).
- `docs/icons-design.md`, `packages/herdr/README.md` — Herdr UI conventions.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required — the seed description ("make the In Review header background gray (or similar) to differentiate that section from other sections") was specific enough to draft the brief directly. Assumption recorded: "gray (or similar)" means a grey ANSI 256 background (default candidate: 238, same value already used elsewhere in `worklist.ts`), applied only to the In Review heading; other section headers remain unchanged. Rationale: description explicitly scopes differentiation to "that section".

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MKW1GUSC1DSWYGS** – OpenCode (completed)
- **WL-0ML1LBF6H0NE40RX** – Fix TUI work item colors: use blessed markup instead of chalk ANSI codes (completed)
- **WL-0ML4DOK1U19NN8LG** – Add wl list --parent <id> for child-only listing (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `CLI.md` — matched: background, extension, header, herdr, list, make, section, sections, selection, similar
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: background, extension, header, herdr, list, make, section, sections, selection
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: background, extension, header, herdr, list, make, section, sections, selection

## Problem

The 1,000-line maintainability ceiling adopted for WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 is
enforced only by review. Evidence of the gap: WL-0MQJK4UJD0028IRO decomposed
`database.ts` from 2,584 lines and closed as shipped, yet
`packages/shared/src/database.ts` is now 3,684 lines — the decomposition never
landed on `main` and nothing flagged the regrowth. The same sweep created 12+
sibling god-class items (WL-0MVGKGD2Y0038S6B, WL-0MVGKGJXJ000ISBU,
WL-0MVGKGMU400631VZ, ...), each of which can regrow the same way.

## Goal

A cheap, deterministic check (script or test) that fails when a source file
exceeds 1,000 lines, with an explicit, shrinking allow-list for grandfathered
files so the check is green from day one and cannot silently regrow.

## Draft acceptance criteria

1. A check exists (script `scripts/check-file-size.ts` or a vitest unit test)
   that reports every non-test source file > 1,000 lines.
2. Grandfathered files are listed explicitly with their current line count, and
   the check fails if a listed file grows beyond its recorded budget.
3. The check is wired into an existing automated gate (pre-push or CI) without
   adding more than ~2 s to that gate.
4. Retiring an entry is required when an item from the WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7
   sweep completes a decomposition.

# Remove dead top-level `singleFork` key in vitest.config.ts

**discovered-from:** WL-0MVF9JJUH0077OB8 — Reduce time to run tests

## Problem statement

`vitest.config.ts` sets `singleFork: true` at the top level of the `test`
block. Vitest 4 has no such top-level option — `singleFork` is a
`poolOptions.forks.*` key — so the setting is silently ignored (no warning is
emitted). The comment directly above it, "Force per-file isolation by limiting
to 1 active worker per file sequence", describes behaviour that is actually
provided by `isolate: true` + `maxWorkers: 4` (+ `pool: 'forks'`).

The dead key is harmless today, but it is misleading: a future reader may
believe the suite is serialised, and a migration to an option shape that *is*
read (or vitest version churn that starts warning) could confuse diagnosis.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `singleFork: true` is removed from `vitest.config.ts`.
- The comment above it is rewritten (or removed) to state what actually
  enforces per-file isolation (`pool: 'forks'`, `isolate: true`,
  `maxWorkers: 4`), and that parallelism is otherwise intentional.
- Full canonical suite (`tests/cli` + `tests/unit`) stays green with the same
  test counts; no runtime regression in either wall-clock or aggregate test
  time on the same host.

## Out of scope

Bumping `maxWorkers` / `fileParallelism` — that is the follow-up "Test-suite
parallelism: reconsider maxWorkers on hosts with more cores".
data.title: vitest.config.ts: remove dead top-level singleFork key (vitest 4 ignores it)

## Goal

As a wl CLI maintainer, I want the new `wl worklist --json` invocation served from and backfilled into the existing on-disk read cache as a single cache entry, so repeat refreshes across Herdr panes hit the cache once per refresh instead of per subset.

## Scope

Parent AC1 (cache half) and AC4 (cache correctness).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `worklist` is added to `READ_CACHE_COMMANDS` and `isCacheableReadCommand('worklist')` returns true.
- A cacheable `wl worklist --json` invocation is served from cache on repeat with an unchanged DB: second invocation records a `cache-hit` spawn (`recordSpawn('cache-hit')`) and performs no DB work.
- A write (create/update/sync/comment…) bumps the state counter and invalidates the worklist entry; the next invocation does real read work and reflects the new DB state.
- The payload is keyed by `(worklog-dir, argv)` exactly like the other read commands — a different `--worklog-dir` or different `-n` count is a distinct entry.
- A mid-action write is not cached: when the state counter changes between lookup and `onJsonOutput`, the payload is not stored (same guard as today's commands).
- `WL_CACHE_DISABLED=1` disables both lookup and backfill for `worklist`.
- The cache serves the new command before the heavy command graph loads (the existing `src/cli.ts` preAction lookup path covers it; no new fast-path exception).
- New tests in `tests/cli/` cover: hit-on-repeat, invalidation-on-write, distinct keys for distinct `--worklog-dir`, and the disable env var.
- Changed-scope tests pass and the full suite stays green.

- Traceability to parent WL-0MVGYLU0S004WZUS AC1: the consolidated `wl worklist --json` invocation is served as one read-cache entry.
- Traceability to parent WL-0MVGYLU0S004WZUS AC4: cache correctness unchanged — identical JSON for identical DB state, write invalidation still bumps the state counter, and worktree / `--worklog-dir` behaviour is unchanged.
- Traceability to parent WL-0MVGYLU0S004WZUS AC6: new tests cover read-cache hit and write-invalidation for the consolidated command.

## Minimal implementation

1. Add `'worklist'` to `READ_CACHE_COMMANDS` in `src/read-cache-cli.ts`.
2. Verify — and adjust if needed — that `shouldCacheReadInvocation('worklist', argv)` returns true in JSON mode with no non-cacheable flags; `worklist` has no write-byproduct flags, so it should already be cacheable once listed.
3. Confirm the `src/cli.ts` / `src/cli-main.ts` lookup paths route the new command (no change expected; tests prove it).
4. Add `tests/cli/worklist-cache.test.ts`.

## Key Files

- `src/read-cache-cli.ts` — add `worklist` to `READ_CACHE_COMMANDS`
- `src/cli.ts`, `src/cli-main.ts` — cache lookup wiring (verify unchanged)
- `tests/cli/worklist-cache.test.ts` — **new** hit/invalidation/keying/disable tests
- `tests/cli/cli-helpers.ts` — fixture (from WL-C1)

## Dependencies

- Depends on WL-C2 (`wl worklist` command must exist and emit the JSON payload the cache stores).

## Deliverables

- `worklist` registered as a cacheable read command.
- Cache hit/invalidation/keying/disable test coverage.
- Verified single-entry-per-(dir, argv) behaviour.

## Notes

- The state-counter fingerprint and write-invalidation machinery are reused unchanged — do NOT fork the cache.
- The mid-action-write guard already exists in `ReadCacheCli.onJsonOutput`; the new tests must prove `worklist` goes through it.

## Goal

As a Herdr plugin maintainer, I want the default-view refresh to issue **one** `wl` read per tick — `wl worklist --json` — with the critical, review-queue, in-progress-root and blocked-root guarantees preserved and a fail-open fallback to today's per-subset spawn path when the consolidated read is unavailable.

## Scope

Parent AC2 (single read), AC5 (output parity), AC6 (fetcher tests).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `fetchNextItems(count)` for a default-view refresh issues exactly **one** `runWl` invocation (`worklist`) when the command is available; no `wl list` or `wl next` spawns are issued for the bundle path (the in-flight fetch memo is bypassed for the bundle, or dedupes it, with no extra spawns).
- The mandatory subsets are derived from the bundle: all critical, all in_review (completed + in-progress), all in-progress roots and all blocked roots appear in the returned list regardless of the browse count (existing mandatory-guarantee tests still pass).
- `fetchReviewQueueState()` is derived from the bundle's `reviewQueue` subset (completed-only count + `auditsOutstanding`) and returns the same value as today's standalone `wl list` query for the same DB state.
- Audit enrichment is preserved: for items shared with mandatory `wl list` subsets, the richer `wl list`-style audit fields (`auditResult`, `auditedAt`, `fingerprint`, `currentFingerprint`) win over the `browse` representation, exactly as today (WL-0MUWDW0N6003KF6G).
- Output parity: for the same DB state, the bundle path's final `selectWorkItems` → `regroupWorkItems` output is identical to today's per-subset path (test compares both pipelines on the seeded fixture).
- Fail-open: when `wl worklist` is unavailable (older `wl`, non-zero exit, malformed/unparseable payload, missing subset key), the fetcher falls back to the existing per-subset spawns with byte-identical behaviour — the fallback path is asserted by a test that mocks the bundle failure.
- `wl next`'s auto re-sort is NOT triggered by the bundle (pure read); no write byproduct, so the result is deterministically cacheable.
- `--worklog-dir` and managed-worktree resolution behave unchanged (existing worktree tests still pass).
- New tests cover: single-spawn assertion, mandatory-subset presence, review-queue derivation, output parity, and fail-open fallback.
- Changed-scope tests pass and the full suite stays green.

- Traceability to parent WL-0MVGYLU0S004WZUS AC2: `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` issues that single read per default-view refresh tick; the mandatory-subset guarantees (critical always shown, blocked always shown, review queue always shown) are preserved by tests.
- Traceability to parent WL-0MVGYLU0S004WZUS AC5: Herdr refresh output is unchanged for the same DB state (existing fetcher tests + the spawn-reduction simulation pass).
- Traceability to parent WL-0MVGYLU0S004WZUS AC6: new tests cover the fetcher's single-spawn path, mandatory-subset guarantees and output parity with the per-subset path.

## Minimal implementation

1. Add `worklist` to the fetcher's `MEMOIZABLE_COMMANDS` set (bundle is a cacheable read; memo dedupes identical concurrent refreshes — same as today).
2. Add `fetchWorklistBundle()` that runs `runWl(['worklist', '-n', String(count)])`, extracts the five subsets with `extractItems`, and validates the shape (unknown-shape ⇒ fail-open).
3. Rework `fetchNextItems(count)` to: try the bundle → derive mandatory sets + review-queue state + browse feed → merge/enrich with the existing `WL-0MUWDW0N6003KF6G` logic → `selectWorkItems` → `regroupWorkItems`; on any failure, fall back to today's `Promise.all([runWl(next), fetchMandatorySubsets()])` exactly.
4. Rework `fetchReviewQueueState()` to read the bundle's `reviewQueue` subset when already fetched in the same refresh, falling back to the standalone query.
5. Add `packages/herdr/src/fetcher-worklist-bundle.test.ts` with injected fake `execFileAsync` covering the criteria.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `fetchWorklistBundle`, reworked `fetchNextItems`, `fetchReviewQueueState`, memo set
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher-worklist-bundle.test.ts` — **new** bundle tests
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher-review-queue.test.ts`, `fetcher-include-blocked.test.ts`, `fetcher-inprocess.test.ts` — existing guarantees must keep passing
- `tests/cli/cli-helpers.ts` — seeded fixture (from WL-C1)

## Dependencies

- Depends on WL-C2 (`wl worklist` command + payload contract) and WL-C3 (cacheability).
- Depends on WL-C1 only transitively via WL-C2 (fixtures land in WL-C1; tests here reuse them).

## Deliverables

- Single-spawn default-view refresh with preserved mandatory guarantees.
- Review-queue state derived from the bundle.
- Fail-open fallback path.
- Fetcher test coverage including output parity.

## Notes

- Keep the browse feed bounded by the caller's count; mandatory subsets stay unfiltered by count.
- The re-sort write-byproduct risk (parent risk, medium) is handled by the command's `--no-re-sort`-style selection (WL-C2) plus this slice's output-parity test; if parity genuinely differs, record it as a comment and resolve separately rather than making the bundle a write.

## Goal

As a Herdr pane operator, I want `doRefresh` to run the whole default-view refresh from the single consolidated read — items, review-queue banner state and actionable context — so a refresh tick costs one `wl` process instead of five per pane.

## Scope

Parent AC2 (wire-through), AC5 (unchanged output), AC6 (worklist-level tests).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A default-view `doRefresh` cycle issues exactly **one** `wl` spawn for worklist data (asserted by a spawn-count integration test with an injected exec seam), down from five.
- The review-queue banner state (`applySprintState`) is populated from the same consolidated read — no separate review-queue spawn on the default view.
- Filtered views are unchanged: the stage-filtered (`fetchItemsByStage`), priority-filtered (`fetchItemsByPriority`) and recent-dispatches paths still use their existing reads, and the `activeDispatchFilter` path still merges live items from the default fetcher.
- Expanded-parent children still render correctly across the swap (no collapse flicker): the batched in-process children read continues to run concurrently with the consolidated item read, and the existing expand-across-refresh test passes.
- Idle behaviour is preserved: a refresh with no change still spawns zero `wl` processes where it did before (no new unconditional read).
- Event-loop responsiveness: the ≤ 100 ms p95 input-lag guard test still passes.
- Fail-open at the TUI layer: when the consolidated read fails, the refresh shows the per-subset fallback result (or the previous list) instead of an empty or errored view.
- New/extended tests cover the single-spawn default view, derived banner state, and unchanged filtered-view behaviour.
- Changed-scope tests pass and the full suite stays green.

- Traceability to parent WL-0MVGYLU0S004WZUS AC2: the default-view refresh issues that single read per default-view refresh tick and the mandatory-subset guarantees are preserved by tests.
- Traceability to parent WL-0MVGYLU0S004WZUS AC5: Herdr refresh output is unchanged for the same DB state; existing fetcher tests and the spawn-reduction simulation pass.

## Minimal implementation

1. In `doRefresh`, replace the `fetchReviewQueueState()` + `fetchItemsForView(...)` default-path pair with one consolidated fetch that yields both the items and the review-queue state (e.g. `fetchWorklistBundle()` returns `{ items, reviewState, actionableCount? }`).
2. Keep the children fetch (`fetchChildrenForItems`) concurrent with the consolidated read via the existing `InProcessRefreshScope`.
3. Keep `fetchItemsForView` for the filtered/dispatch views; only the unfiltered default path changes.
4. Extend the worklist refresh test(s) with a spawn-count assertion using the injected `setExecFileAsync` seam.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `doRefresh` wiring, `applySprintState` input
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — bundle result shape consumed by `doRefresh` (from WL-C4)
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-*.test.ts` — single-spawn + banner + filtered-view coverage
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-expand-refresh.test.ts` — must keep passing

## Dependencies

- Depends on WL-C4 (fetcher bundle + fail-open fallback).

## Deliverables

- Default-view refresh driven by one consolidated read.
- Banner state derived from the same read.
- Single-spawn and unchanged-filtered-view test coverage.

## Notes

- "One spawn" means one **worklist-data** spawn per tick. The in-process SQLite reads (children, actionable count) are already zero-spawn and stay that way.
- Do not reorder or bypass `doRefresh`'s typing gate, visibility gate, single-flight guard or trailing coalescing.

## Goal

As a maintainer, I want the documentation and measured benchmark evidence updated to describe the consolidated read, so the next engineer can see what changed, why, the measured CPU reduction against the F10 baseline, and how to reproduce it.

## Scope

Parent AC3 (measurement evidence) and AC7 (documentation).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` § "Cold-refresh cost" describes the consolidated read: one `wl worklist --json` per default-view tick, one read-cache entry, review-queue/browse derivation, the fail-open fallback, and that filtered views are unchanged.
- `CLI.md` documents `wl worklist` — purpose, options (`-n/--number`, `--prefix`), JSON payload shape (five subsets + metadata), pure-read/cacheable guarantee, and a usage example.
- Inline doc comments in `src/commands/worklist.ts`, `src/read-cache-cli.ts` (`READ_CACHE_COMMANDS` comment) and `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` reflect the new path, cross-referencing the same rationale as the docs.
- The measured spawn count per default-view refresh is recorded in the doc (expected 5 → 1) and produced by the harness, not hand-waved.
- `bench/herdr-refresh-cycle.ts --query-set consolidated --json --items 20 --cycle-seconds 30 --tick-seconds 5` is executed and its CPU-seconds-per-cycle result is recorded on this work item and in the doc, compared against the pre-F4 baseline (159.44 CPU-s) and the F10 target (≤ 63.78 CPU-s).
